quote: Wie vieler solcher Darstellungen giebt es? (Verallgemeinerung des Syl- vesterschen Trägheitsgesetzes für und dasselbe für quater- näre etc Formen)
english: How many such representations are there? (Generalization of Sylvester's law of inertia, and the same for quaternary etc. forms.)
topic: A list of research notes: upper bounds for the coefficients of the characteristic function following Noether, representations of a multiple of a ternary form as a sum of three squares, counting contact curves via Abelian functions, and finiteness of integral invariants of an integral linear substitution.

triage.modern_statement: Context on the page: a nonnegative (positive semidefinite) real ternary form f, or a suitable multiple of it, written as a sum of three squares of forms, f = p1^2 + p2^2 + p3^2. Hilbert (1888) proved this for ternary quartics, and his 1893 Acta Math. paper extended it to multiples of psd ternary forms of higher degree. The question is how many essentially different representations exist, counting two as the same if they differ by a real orthogonal transformation of (p1, p2, p3). He frames this as a higher-degree version of Sylvester's law of inertia (which pins down the sum-of-squares/signature data of a quadratic form) and asks the same for quaternary and higher forms. The nearby note about counting contact curves with Abelian functions suggests he wanted to count the representations through the contact curves of f = 0 (for quartics, the bitangent / Steiner-complex structure).
triage.answered_by: Only partly answered. For the main case, general ternary quartics, V. Powers, B. Reznick, C. Scheiderer and F. Sottile, 'A new approach to Hilbert's theorem on ternary quartics', C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris 339 (2004), 617–620. They showed a general quartic has exactly 63 inequivalent representations as a sum of three squares over C, and a general nonnegative one has 8 over R. Blekherman, Smith and Velasco (IMRN 2019, arXiv:1606.04387) extended the count to sum-of-squares representations of general quadratic forms on all surfaces of minimal degree. I did not find a source giving a full count for Hilbert's 1893 higher-degree ternary multiples, or for quaternary forms in general.

evidence.claim: Hilbert (1888) proved that every nonnegative real ternary quartic is a sum of three squares of quadratic forms.
In 1893 Hilbert generalized the 1888 result ('Ueber ternäre definite Formen', Acta Math. 17 (1893), 169–197).
Powers, Reznick, Scheiderer and Sottile showed a general ternary quartic is a sum of three squares in exactly 63 essentially different ways over C, and a general nonnegative one in eight ways over R.
Publication details: Powers, Reznick, Scheiderer, Sottile, 'A new approach to Hilbert's theorem on ternary quartics', C. R. Math. Acad. Sci. Paris 339 (2004), 617–620.

The 2019 paper on low-rank sum-of-squares representations counts equivalence classes of representations of general quadratic forms on surfaces of minimal degree, generalizing the ternary-quartic count, and shows there are only finitely many inequivalent representations.

triage.why: The page's topics (multiples of ternary forms as sums of three squares, contact curves) clearly point to Hilbert's 1888/1893 work on representing psd ternary forms as sums of squares. 'How many such representations?' was answered for general ternary quartics in 2004 (63 over C, 8 over R), and the count was later extended to varieties of minimal degree, so the area is still being worked on. It is not one of Hilbert's 23 problems, though it is related to the 17th. Medium confidence for three reasons: the note is short; it may be about the higher-degree multiples from 1893, for which I found no complete count; and the quaternary part has, per the sources I found, only partial answers.
